methodology.note: V3.1 keeps raw capital/activity observations separate from strategic scores, adds geography and time-horizon context, evidence-derived confidence, driver-based scenarios, rank robustness, live hero anchors, immutable history, change-only publishing, and a review-gated source-discovery workflow. Cross-sector money measures remain intentionally non-comparable.

formulas.Overall Opportunity: Weighted average of positive dimensions minus a hype-risk penalty. User adjustable.
formulas.Market Attractiveness: Capital, momentum, durability, business value, defensibility, value capture, entrepreneurship and confidence, with hype penalty.
formulas.Career Attractiveness: Income, scarcity, AI resilience, business value, transferability, optionality, accessibility, value capture and durability.
formulas.Personal Fit: If no preference dimensions are activated, Personal Fit equals Career Attractiveness. Active preferences contribute a weighted intensity-match component; untouched sliders contribute zero information.
formulas.Context adjustment: Selected objective is blended with geography (10%) and selected time-horizon thesis (15%); the underlying objective remains 75%.
formulas.Confidence: Calculated from source quality, source count, source diversity, recency and evidence directness for the exact opportunity node.
formulas.Robustness: Monte Carlo simulation perturbs evidence-based scores according to confidence; Overall Opportunity also perturbs user weights. Output is Top-5 probability, median rank and 10–90% rank range.

methodology.rawCapitalRule: Raw capital observations are displayed with their flow type and status. They are not summed or ranked directly across unlike categories such as government expenditure, technology spending, industry sales, VC/M&A, or cumulative infrastructure requirements.

nodes.name: AI Infrastructure & Inference Systems
nodes.thesis: The strongest pure-tech capital wave: the bottleneck shifts from model novelty toward reliable, efficient inference, serving, orchestration and cost control.
nodes.evidence: $1.43T 2026 AI-infrastructure spend; major tech capex is accelerating and enterprise AI usage is moving into production.
path: Foundation
Master Linux, networking, Python/C++, cloud primitives and distributed-systems fundamentals.
Practitioner
Deploy and benchmark inference stacks; build observability, batching, caching and cost/latency experiments.
Specialist
Own multi-GPU serving, reliability and performance; understand hardware/software co-design and economics.
Leverage
Move into principal architecture, platform leadership, infra consulting, developer infrastructure or product ownership.
nodes.counter: Hyperscaler concentration and rapid model-efficiency gains could compress infrastructure margins; tooling layers can commoditize quickly.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if hyperscaler AI capex contracts for multiple years, inference demand grows slower than efficiency gains, and accelerator scarcity disappears without creating new workload demand.
nodes.valueChain: Accelerators → networking → orchestration → inference runtime → observability → enterprise workloads

nodes.name: Data Centers, Power & Thermal Systems
nodes.thesis: AI's physical bottleneck. Power delivery, cooling, electrical equipment and high-density data-center design can capture value even if model vendors change.
nodes.evidence: >$650B 2026 data-center spending; nearly $7T cumulative data-center investment may be required through 2030; power/thermal equipment are cited constraints.
path: Foundation
Build power, thermal, controls and data-center architecture fundamentals.
Practitioner
Model rack density, cooling, redundancy, energy efficiency and capacity trade-offs.
Specialist
Own high-density AI-facility design or critical equipment/product domains.
Leverage
Lead infrastructure programs, equipment businesses, advisory, project development or investment platforms.
nodes.counter: Project pipelines can be overbuilt; permitting, grid delays and financing costs can strand planned capacity.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if AI utilization materially disappoints, power-density growth stalls, and data-center vacancy rises persistently across major regions.
nodes.valueChain: Grid interconnect → transformers/switchgear → UPS/power electronics → cooling → facility → compute

nodes.name: Grid, Power Systems & Electrification
nodes.thesis: A structural infrastructure supercycle: electricity demand, grid congestion, energy security, storage and electrification make power-system expertise unusually durable.
nodes.evidence: $3.4T global energy investment expected in 2026 (+5%); ~$2.2T into clean energy. Energy/power alone represents a large share of future infrastructure need.
path: Foundation
Learn circuits, power systems, energy markets and grid operations.
Practitioner
Build forecasting/optimization projects around load, storage or network congestion.
Specialist
Own a scarce bottleneck: interconnection, grid software, power electronics, storage optimization or protection.
Leverage
Move into principal engineering, energy-tech product leadership, project development, advisory or infrastructure ownership.
nodes.counter: Returns depend heavily on regulation, permitting and project execution; some subsectors are low-margin despite huge spending.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if electricity-demand growth structurally reverses and grid/energy capex plans are cancelled rather than delayed.
nodes.valueChain: Generation → transmission → grid software → storage → distribution → electrified loads

nodes.name: AI Security, Identity & Cyber Resilience
nodes.thesis: Security remains non-discretionary while AI creates new attack surfaces, machine identities, agent permissions and governance problems.
nodes.evidence: $244B information-security spending in 2026 (+11.6%); AI cybersecurity spending is rising much faster within the broader market.
path: Foundation
Master networks, OS, identity, cloud and secure software fundamentals.
Practitioner
Build threat models and labs for cloud, APIs and AI agents; learn detection and response.
Specialist
Own machine identity, AI security, cloud security architecture or application security.
Leverage
Progress to security architect/CISO-track, specialist consulting, security product or founder roles.
nodes.counter: Security tools are crowded, procurement is consolidating and some operational work will be automated by AI.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if security budgets become discretionary and AI meaningfully reduces net attack surface faster than it creates new complexity.
nodes.valueChain: Identity → policy → application/cloud controls → AI/agent controls → detection/response → governance

nodes.name: Enterprise AI Architecture & Agentic Automation
nodes.thesis: The monetization layer: enterprises need AI connected to processes, data, controls and measurable economics—not isolated demos.
nodes.evidence: 2026 AI services $585.5B and AI software $453.2B; agentic AI is beginning to disrupt traditional enterprise application economics.
path: Foundation
Learn AI/LLM architecture, APIs, data, enterprise processes and value-case fundamentals.
Practitioner
Automate a real workflow with controls, evaluation, human-in-the-loop and measurable ROI.
Specialist
Own cross-system agent architecture, enterprise AI governance and production rollout.
Leverage
Move into principal architecture, transformation leadership, specialist consulting, vertical AI product or founder roles.
nodes.counter: Generic implementation work can commoditize quickly and incumbent platforms can absorb standalone features.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if enterprises fail to move agents into production or if implementation becomes near-zero-friction and value capture shifts entirely to platform vendors.
nodes.valueChain: Models/platforms → data/integration → business process → governance → measurable outcomes

nodes.name: AI Semiconductors, Memory & Advanced Packaging
nodes.thesis: Compute scarcity and strategic sovereignty make accelerators, HBM, packaging, chip design and manufacturing equipment high-barrier value pools.
nodes.evidence: SIA reported $791.7B of global semiconductor sales in 2025. In June 2026, SIA endorsed the WSTS forecast for more than $1.5T of 2026 sales; by July, year-to-date sales had already exceeded the prior full-year record.
path: Foundation
Build serious electrical/computer engineering, digital logic and architecture depth.
Practitioner
Design/verify FPGA or ASIC blocks; learn memory hierarchy and performance modeling.
Specialist
Own accelerator, memory, packaging, verification or EDA bottlenecks.
Leverage
Advance to principal/chief architect, semiconductor IP, EDA, fabless startup or strategic technical leadership.
nodes.counter: The sector is cyclical, geopolitically exposed and extremely capital intensive; not all parts capture equal economics.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if AI compute demand plateaus for years and capacity oversupply structurally destroys pricing across accelerators, memory and foundry layers.

nodes.name: Defense AI, Drones & Autonomous Systems
nodes.thesis: European rearmament plus autonomy, sensing, cyber and software-defined systems are redirecting both public spending and venture capital.
nodes.evidence: $2.887T global military spending in 2025; Europe +14%. European defense/security/resilience startup VC hit $8.7B in 2025 (+55%).
path: Foundation
Build robotics/embedded/AI fundamentals and understand defense system constraints.
Practitioner
Ship perception, autonomy, simulation or secure-communications prototypes.
Specialist
Own mission-critical autonomy, sensor fusion, EW-adjacent software or resilient edge systems.
Leverage
Move into technical leadership, defense product, dual-use startup or mission-systems architecture.
nodes.counter: Procurement cycles, export controls and political priorities can be unpredictable; ethical and jurisdictional constraints matter.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if European procurement plans reverse materially and autonomous/software-defined defense fails to gain budget share.
nodes.valueChain: Sensors → edge compute → autonomy → communications → command systems → procurement/operations

nodes.name: Robotics & Industrial Automation
nodes.thesis: AI moves from digital work into the physical economy. The moat comes from integrating perception, controls, hardware, safety and real operations.
nodes.evidence: 542k industrial robots were installed globally in 2024—more than double a decade earlier; US installations rose 11% in 2025.
path: Foundation
Build mechanics/controls/programming and probability/linear algebra foundations.
Practitioner
Create a real or simulated robot stack: perception → planning → control.
Specialist
Own a hard layer such as perception, manipulation, autonomy, safety or factory integration.
Leverage
Lead robotics platforms, industrial automation programs, product companies or specialist integration businesses.
nodes.counter: Hardware cycles are slow, unit economics can be difficult and humanoid hype may outrun deployment reality.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if real-world deployment economics remain inferior to human labor across most target workflows for an extended period.
nodes.valueChain: Sensors/actuators → embedded/controls → perception/planning → safety → workflow integration

nodes.name: AI Data Infrastructure, Retrieval & Governance
nodes.thesis: AI increases the value of trusted, governed, searchable proprietary data. The durable work is architecture, quality, lineage, retrieval and operational data systems—not dashboards.
nodes.evidence: AI-data spending is growing from a small base while enterprise AI and cloud budgets expand sharply; demand is reinforced by AI adoption and governance requirements.
path: Foundation
Master SQL, Python, data modeling, distributed systems and cloud basics.
Practitioner
Build batch + streaming pipelines, retrieval systems and quality/lineage controls.
Specialist
Own AI-ready data architecture, semantic/retrieval platforms or governed data products.
Leverage
Move into principal data architecture, platform products, specialist consulting or vertical data businesses.
nodes.counter: Platform vendors can commoditize individual tooling; weak data programs often become governance-heavy without clear ROI.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if enterprise AI ceases to depend materially on proprietary data quality, integration and governance.
nodes.valueChain: Sources → pipelines/streaming → storage/modeling → search/retrieval → governance → AI/apps

nodes.name: Cloud, Distributed Systems & Platform Engineering
nodes.thesis: Cloud remains the operating substrate for AI and enterprise systems. Durable value sits in reliability, architecture, performance, cost and developer platforms.
nodes.evidence: Global IT spend is forecast at $6.37T in 2026; AI-optimized IaaS alone is forecast at $42B, +96%.
path: Foundation
Master Linux, networks, one systems language, cloud and databases.
Practitioner
Operate production services; build IaC, observability, CI/CD and failure testing.
Specialist
Own reliability, distributed architecture, platform engineering or cloud economics at scale.
Leverage
Advance to principal engineering, platform leadership, infrastructure product or consulting.
nodes.counter: Managed services and AI coding tools will commoditize routine infrastructure work; value concentrates at scale and complexity.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if cloud complexity collapses materially and reliability/performance become largely autonomous commodities.
nodes.valueChain: Compute/network/storage → cloud primitives → platform → developer experience → applications

nodes.name: Computational Biology & AI-enabled Biotech
nodes.thesis: A high-risk, high-moat intersection where AI can accelerate discovery, but true value requires biology, experimentation, regulation and clinical translation.
nodes.evidence: Biotech financing reached $68.5B in 2025 (+11%); biopharma VC was $12.6B in H1 2026 and M&A activity is strengthening.
path: Foundation
Build serious biology plus statistics/programming depth; do not treat biology as a dataset only.
Practitioner
Reproduce computational biology work and contribute to experimentally grounded projects.
Specialist
Own a high-value layer: protein/sequence modeling, multimodal biology, translational analytics or computational chemistry.
Leverage
Lead scientific platforms, biotech R&D, technology strategy, venture creation or IP-driven companies.
nodes.counter: Science risk, clinical failure, regulation and long capital cycles are much harsher than software; AI-only differentiation is fragile.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if computational methods fail to improve experimental/clinical productivity or capital markets structurally retreat from biotech innovation.
nodes.valueChain: Biological data → models → experiments → preclinical/clinical → regulatory → commercialization

nodes.name: Financial Infrastructure & Fintech
nodes.thesis: Payments, risk, compliance, treasury and market infrastructure remain valuable because they sit directly on money movement and regulation.
nodes.evidence: $103.1B global fintech investment in H1 2026 vs $72.2B in H2 2025; VC was $31.5B and M&A drove much of the increase.
path: Foundation
Learn software/data systems plus financial statements, payments, credit/risk and regulation.
Practitioner
Build a ledger, payments/risk workflow or financial-data system with auditability.
Specialist
Own a money-adjacent bottleneck: payments infra, fraud, treasury, regtech, risk or market data.
Leverage
Move into product/architecture, fintech leadership, specialist consulting, founder or investment roles.
nodes.counter: Fintech is highly regulated, competitive and vulnerable to distribution advantages held by banks/platform incumbents.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if funding remains concentrated in megadeals while new-category formation and durable unit economics deteriorate broadly.

nodes.name: Quantitative Research & AI in Markets
nodes.thesis: One of the highest employee-compensation ceilings, driven by direct value capture from forecasting, execution and risk—but access is exceptionally selective.
nodes.evidence: Career economics are stronger than transparent sector-flow data here; treat the capital-flow score as a proxy rather than a directly comparable market-spend metric.
path: Foundation
Reach exceptional probability, statistics, algorithms and programming competence.
Practitioner
Run rigorous research on noisy time-series data; learn leakage, execution and transaction-cost realism.
Specialist
Develop alpha/risk/execution expertise or low-latency systems depth.
Leverage
Progress to senior researcher/PM, systematic platform leadership, prop trading or capital allocation.
nodes.counter: Extremely selective, performance-driven and capacity constrained; success distribution is very unequal.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if your realistic probability of entry remains low after serious evidence-based testing of math/research ability.

nodes.name: Advanced Manufacturing & Industrial Software
nodes.thesis: Reshoring, automation and supply-chain resilience increase demand for software that touches real production, quality, maintenance and factory economics.
nodes.evidence: Deep tech reached 32% of European VC in 2025; Europe attracted $20B (+21%) while US deep-tech funding reached $144B (+92%).
path: Foundation
Learn manufacturing operations plus software/data architecture and industrial protocols.
Practitioner
Connect machines/OT data to analytics, quality, maintenance or production workflows.
Specialist
Own OT/IT architecture, industrial AI, digital twins or software-defined production systems.
Leverage
Lead factory transformation, industrial software products, specialist consulting or vertical SaaS/AI businesses.
nodes.counter: Industrial sales cycles are long and integration-heavy; legacy environments can slow product scaling.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if reshoring/automation capex weakens structurally and industrial software remains unable to produce measurable productivity gains.
nodes.valueChain: Machines/controls → OT data → MES/MOM → analytics/AI → ERP/supply chain → economics

nodes.name: Infrastructure Finance & Private Capital
nodes.thesis: The ownership layer of the infrastructure supercycle: those who can underwrite, structure, finance and operate scarce assets can capture value beyond salaries.
nodes.evidence: Infrastructure fundraising reached a record ~$200B in 2025 (+58% YoY); an estimated $106T of infrastructure investment is needed through 2040.
path: Foundation
Master accounting, corporate finance, valuation and project-finance mechanics.
Practitioner
Build investment cases for energy, data centers or digital/transport infrastructure.
Specialist
Develop sector underwriting depth and transaction/operating experience.
Leverage
Move toward investment committee, fund leadership, development platforms, GP economics or direct ownership.
nodes.counter: Access is networked and competitive; returns can be damaged by leverage, cost overruns and regulatory shifts.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if infrastructure fundraising and realized returns weaken persistently while required capex is increasingly financed at unattractive economics.
nodes.valueChain: Capital raising → underwriting → financing → development/build → operations → asset ownership

nodes.name: Critical Infrastructure & Resilience Technology
nodes.thesis: A quieter intersection of physical infrastructure, climate adaptation, cyber-physical resilience and public-sector modernization with long-duration demand.
nodes.evidence: $106T infrastructure need through 2040; energy and digital infrastructure account for a large portion and private capital is increasing allocations.
path: Foundation
Build systems, risk, infrastructure and data/security fundamentals.
Practitioner
Model failure modes and resilience for a real physical-digital system.
Specialist
Own a cross-domain bottleneck in utilities, water, transport, telecom or public infrastructure.
Leverage
Lead resilience programs, critical-infrastructure products, advisory or infrastructure operations.
nodes.counter: Budgets can be fragmented and procurement slow; value may accrue to large incumbents rather than specialists.
nodes.changeMind: Downgrade if infrastructure owners stop treating resilience as a funded priority despite rising physical/digital dependency.
nodes.valueChain: Physical assets → sensing/data → risk/security → operations → public/private financing
